scenes.title: The lens splits the room into zones
The PIR sensor sees a heat change
A relay switches the light on

vo.text: You walk into a dark room, and the light turns on by itself.
A small motion sensor on the wall made that decision.
Behind its window, a Fresnel lens focuses invisible heat from your body onto a sensor.
The lens divides the room into separate zones, so movement creates a changing pattern.
A PIR sensor compares the heat in different windows and detects that change.
When the pattern shifts enough, the sensor sends a brief trigger signal.
A controller uses that signal to close a relay and power the light.
So focused heat, a changing pattern, and a relay turn your movement into light.
